Nick Lakin.b:
Nick Lakin enters his sixth season as UNI swimming and diving head coach in 2022.
During his tenure, UNI has won two relay events and thirteen individual conference titles. Eleven different swimmers have received first team All-MVC honors, including Crystal Florman who captured MVC Swimmer of the Year honors in 2019.
In 2018-19, Lakin guided UNI to a fourth place finish at the MVC Championships in Columbia, Missouri. Seven swimmers earned first team or honorable mention All-MVC honors. Katie Taylor was awarded the Elite 17 award for athletics and academic performance.
The Panthers collected victories in the 200 and 400 medley relays, breaking school records in both races. Florman won three individual events en route to Swimmer of the Year honors. Taylor and Moriah Ross claimed two individual titles each.
During his first season at the helm, Lakin led the Panthers to a third place finish at the MVC Championships in Iowa City. Nine swimmers and divers earned first team or honorable mention All-MVC honors including two-event champion Katie Taylor.
Six school records fell during the 2017-18 season. Taylor broke the conference record in the 400 individual medley at the MVC Championships.
Diver Izzy Bunchek competed in the NCAA Zone competition.
Prior to UNI, Lakin served as the head coach and program director for the Black Hawk Area Swim Team. Beginning in 2003, he designed and implemented competitive swimming progressions for more than 200 athletes aged 5-22. He developed and maintained working relationships with area high school coaches, local organizations and donors. During his time, Lakin developed more than 50 athletes who progressed to the collegiate level.
He designed recruiting and marketing plans for new athletes along with retention reports to track the progress of his team. Lakin developed booster and sponsor programs that have increased alumni and community involvement. He also oversaw a club communication program that has increased knowledge and support with athletes and families.
Lakin has served the Iowa Swim Coaches Association Board of Directors president and vice president. He was honored as the Iowa Senior Coach of the Year in 2006, 2007, 2011, 2012 and 2013. He and his staff have been named the Age Group Staff of the Year in 2012, 2014, 2015 and 2016.
He earned his bachelor’s degree in advertising at Marist College in 2002. Lakin was a 10-time conference champion and was a four-time conference all-academic selection as a swimming student-athlete. He captained the men’s team to a top-10 mid-major ranking and two conference titles.
Nick lives in Cedar Falls with his wife Jennifer, and their three boys, Trey (14), Maddax (10), and Crosby (8).

Bethany Hovland.b:
Bethany Hovland took over as the head diving coach for the UNI Panthers in August 2018.
Hovland earned the MVC Diving Coach of the Year recognition in 2022 after coaching diver Taylor Hogan to a three-meter conference title, a third-place finish on one-meter and MVC Diver of the Year honors. She was again named the MVC Co-Diving Coach of the Year in 2025 after a strong performance by the Panthers at the conference championships.
In 2026, Hovland earned her third MVC Diving Coach of the Year awrard after an impressive performance by UNI with Avery Hogan winning the three-meter conference title and finishing second in the one-meter. Four divers qualified for the one-meter A-final under Hovland's leadership, marking the first time in program history UNI placed four athletes into the top final for either a swimming or diving event.
Hovland found success during the 2021-2022 season where three of her divers placed in the A final on 1 meter at the MVC Conference Championships and two divers earned honorable mention conference recognition.
During the 2019-2020 season, two of Coach Hovland’s divers earned Missouri Valley Conference Diver of the Week honors. At the Missouri Valley Conference Championships in 2020, Bethany led freshman diver Anna Penning to a top 8 finish, earning her the Missouri Valley Conference Freshman Diver of the Year title.
Upon her hire in July 2018, Hovland still held the 1-meter and 3-meter school records at the University of Northern Iowa. She was the 1-meter Missouri Valley Conference Champion in 2011, making her the first diver in school history to win a conference title. After making four-straight appearances at the NCAA Zone Diving Championships, the "Bethany Hovland Diver of the Year" award was established in her honor in 2013.
Hovland is the founder and head coach of Cedar Valley Diving Club, where she trains divers ages 8-18 years old. She coached high school diving from 2013-17. During her high school coaching career, she coached a two-time state champion along with multiple state qualifiers and finishers, including athletes who continued their diving careers at the collegiate level.
As a native of Cedar Falls, Hovland began her diving career at Cedar Falls High School where she held the 6 and 11 dive school records. She was a two-time Iowa High School State Champion and earned All-American status in 2009.
Hovland earned her bachelor's degree in elementary education from the University of Northern Iowa in 2013 and her master's degree in teaching at Morningside College in 2017. Bethany lives in Cedar Falls, Iowa with her husband Nolan, and their three kids, Benson (5), Laina (3), and Josiah (1).

Ben Colin.b:
The UNI Swimming and Diving team has announced the hiring of Ben Colin as the team’s Assistant Coach.
“Throughout the process Ben demonstrated his passion for UNI and swimming in the state of Iowa”, stated head swimming and diving coach Nick Lakin. “Ben is well known and universally liked, has been a part of the swimming community in the state of Iowa for decades and will bring a ton of enthusiasm and knowledge to the position. We are so thankful to have Ben joining us on deck this year and excited for the future of UNI swimming and diving.”
Colin, a Dubuque, Iowa native, joins the UNI staff after a four year swimming career at the University of Iowa and most recently coached with the Dubuque Area Swimmin’ Hurricanes. While at the University of Iowa Colin earned his degree in Sport & Recreation Management and Journalism, & Mass Communications. He was a three time Big Ten Distinguished Scholar and served as the chair of the Iowa Student Athlete Advisory Committee.
A key contributor to the Panthers' success in the pool, Colin has been responsible for the development of a para swimming training program for UNI student-athletes Olivia Chambers and later Cali Prochaska as both competed on the para swimming circuit both nationally and internationally. Colin was selected to the United States coaching staff for the 2023 Para Swimming World Championships in Manchester, England, as well as the 2024 Paralympic Games in Paris, France.
While at Iowa, Colin was named the 2019 NCAA Jim McKay Scholar for excellence in sport communication. He was active in Iowa Swimming, Inc as a representative on the governance and technical planning committees.

Faith Larsen.b:
Faith Larsen joined the UNI swimming and diving coaching staff ahead of the 2025-26 season, with focus in coaching Panther sprinters.
A three-time All-Missouri Valley Conference (MVC) performer, Larsen was among UNI's top sprinters, becoming the first three-time individual conference champion in program history with titles in the 50-yard freestyle in 2023, 2024 and 2025, while also winning the 100-yard freestyle crown as a senior.
She finished her career with three school records in the 50-yard freestyle (22.34), the 200-yard freestyle relay (1:30.71) and the 400-yard freestyle (3:19.16). Larsen also finished her college career ranked in the top-ten in school history in eight events.
Larsen continues to compete at the club level. In July 2026, she made her international debut at the FISU America Games in Peru, winning two gold medals in the mixed and women's 400-meter freestyle relays, plus one silver (50-meter freestyle) and one bronze medal (50-meter butterfly).
